title: Brown women's soccer falls to Dartmouth 2-1 despite Birtwistle's goal
text:
Sports
Brown women’s soccer falls to Dartmouth 2-1 despite Birtwistle’s goal
Brown University women's soccer lost to Dartmouth College 2-1 despite an early lead from Brooke Birtwistle's goal. The Bears outshot their opponent but could not overcome two unanswered goals by Dartmouth.
Junior defender Brooke Birtwistle scored her fifth goal in as many games, but Brown University women's soccer lost to Dartmouth College, 2-1, on Saturday night at Burnham Field in Hanover. The Bears (8-3-2, 2-1-1 Ivy) took the lead in the 20th minute before Dartmouth (9-2-2, 3-1-0 Ivy) responded with goals late in the first half and early in the second.
The match featured two of the top teams in the Ivy League standings. Brown struck first when senior Joy Okonye delivered a corner kick from the right side that found Birtwistle at the far post for a finish. Dartmouth equalized just before halftime after Natasha Udebhulu converted a loose ball from close range following a free kick into Brown's penalty area. In the 51st minute, Maeve Theobald crossed from the right to Emmanuella Frimpomaa, who scored what proved to be the winning goal.
Despite outshooting Dartmouth 13-6 and leading shots on goal by six to three, Brown was unable to find another equalizer. Among field players for Brown, Birtwistle along with seniors Audrey Lam and Claire Silverman and juniors Kyra Treanor and Chesney Robinson played all ninety minutes. Sophomore goalkeeper Addison Etter made one save during the match.
Dartmouth entered ranked fifth nationally with a goals-against average of 0.417 and remains unbeaten at home this season (7-0). With this win, Dartmouth moved into a tie for first place in conference standings alongside Harvard and Columbia; each has nine points while Brown is two points behind with seven.
Birtwistle has now tallied four goals across four Ivy League games this year and has accounted for each of Brown's last three road goals after scoring twice against Penn earlier this month. Looking ahead, Brown will host Harvard on Saturday, Oct. 24 at Stevenson-Pincince Field.
